title: Kapporot
program_note:
“Kapporot,” or “kapporos,” refers to an ancient and (considered by some to be) somewhat barbaric custom practiced in the past by Jews shortly before the High Holidays — the Days of Atonement.  It involves ritually slaughtering or sacrificing a chicken by swinging it over ones head to “absorb” the sins of the person, thereby absolving him or her.  In this piece, “kapporot” refers to a more personal type of sacrifice relating to the history of part of my family.

The work is structured around the two opposing choirs:  the double- versus single-reeds.  It begins with the mournful double-reeds, interrupted by angry “railing” clarinets.  The mourning and railing eventually coalesce into an urgent prayer...which is finally answered.

The total duration of the composition is approximately 12’30”.
